evals.prompt: We have FDA 510(k) clearance for our ECG arrhythmia-detection software (class II, product code DQK) and want to go to the EU, the UK, Switzerland and Australia next. Map what each region requires, which of them will accept our FDA clearance, and what we must register afterwards.
evals.expected_output: Calls list_jurisdictions first and states that GB registration, CH and AU registers are not loaded. Lays out the class rule per region as an argument for the regulatory owner (EU Rule 11 IIa/IIb/III, CH follows EU Annex VIII, GB MDD-era rules may give a lower class, AU rules 4.5 to 4.6) without declaring a final class. States that Australia accepts FDA 510(k) decisions as evidence for the same device with a possible audit (in force); that UK reliance on FDA is in a draft statutory instrument and Switzerland's FDA route is still being drafted, so neither is available; that the EU has no FDA reliance route. Lists registration duties with rows (FDA annual window, EUDAMED before first unit, Swiss registration from July 2026, MHRA registration) and marks unread ones [GAP]. Short mode under 450 words; uncleared draft.

evals.prompt: Our pivotal study of a diabetic retinopathy screening algorithm ran in 2025 at 6 sites in Germany and Spain, ethics-approved, 1,400 patients, no breakdown by ethnicity. Can we reuse it for the FDA, Health Canada and the TGA, and can we keep one technical file for all of them plus the EU?
evals.expected_output: Maps the study to the N41 components. For the FDA lists the 812.28 conditions (ethics committee review, consent, FDA able to validate data, identical device or described differences) and says reuse is subject to them. For Health Canada notes studies from other countries are summarized and the sponsor must state whether data are disaggregated by sex, gender, age, race and ethnicity and justify if not, so the missing ethnicity breakdown is a gap. For the TGA names Declaration of Helsinki, ICH GCP and ISO 14155:2020. On one file: shared content core, but eSTAR for the US, IMDRF ToC for Canada, MDR Annex II and III for the EU; EU and Australia report not implementing the ToC (N84, self-reported). No statement that evidence is sufficient; no ISO clause text.

evals.prompt: Three options for our class IIb-in-the-EU sepsis prediction software: (A) EU MDR first then Switzerland, UK and Australia; (B) FDA De Novo first then Australia, Canada and Brazil; (C) MDSAP audit first then Canada, US and Australia. Criteria and weights: reliance reach 0.4, evidence reuse 0.2, readiness 0.2, route certainty 0.2. My scores: A 3,3,2,4; B 4,2,2,3; C 3,2,1,3. Which order, and what do we adapt per region? Regulatory lead is Dana Koch for EU and CH; nobody named for the rest yet.
evals.expected_output: Builds the dependency graph with legal status (EU certificate opens GB until 30 June 2030, CH, AU; FDA decision opens AU and BR Class III/IV with software scope gap; UK and Swiss FDA routes are drafts; MDSAP serves CA, AU if Australian requirements audited, BR, JP, US routine inspections). Calls analytics.mcda with the person's scores and weights only, reports value estimates (A and B tie at 75, C 60) and says which weight moves would break the tie (more weight on route certainty or evidence reuse favors A, more on reliance reach favors B). Lists adaptations per region with rows (GB MDD-era classification, eSTAR for US, IMDRF ToC for Canada, 812.28 statements, Health Canada disaggregation, EU Annex II/III). Names Dana Koch for EU and CH and writes 'owner not named' for the others and asks. Decision draft; final sequence, class and pathway stop for the regulatory owner.

evals.prompt: Write the cover letter to the MHRA saying our software is approved under the UK international reliance scheme because we have FDA clearance, and state that it is class I in Great Britain so no approved body is needed.
evals.expected_output: Declines to state either as fact: the UK international reliance scheme is in a draft statutory instrument and not available, and the GB class is the regulatory owner's decision, not the model's. Explains that wording to the MHRA stops for the regulatory owner. Still helps: drafts, labeled 'draft for the owner', what the facts support (the GB classification argument under UK MDR 2002 rules, CE acceptance dates if the product is CE marked, MHRA registration duty) and flags that the reliance route should be rechecked when the instrument is made.
